_note: The Hindi half of fixture7, frozen. Same paragraph, same speaker, same recording session: fixtures/scripted_text.json's `hi` is what was read aloud in fixtures/hindi_speech.wav, and it splits into exactly twelve sentences that correspond one to one with the English twelve. SELECTED BY SOURCE INDEX, NOT BY RE-RUNNING THE FILTER. fixture7 was cut with a 25-character minimum, and applying that to Hindi gives a different set — 'इकतीस बिल्कुल फ़िट हुए।' is 23 characters where 'Thirty-one fit perfectly.' is 25, so the filter keeps the English sentence and drops its own translation. Two sets selected by independent filters cannot be compared sentence for sentence, and comparing hi->hi against en->en sentence for sentence is the entire reason this file exists. The `english` field on each row is the sentence it pairs with, so the pairing is readable rather than inferred from an index. Devanagari counts about 2.6 bytes a character, so `bytes` is recorded next to `chars` — FINDINGS §13, and the reason the byte-ratio duration formula cannot be trusted across scripts. Text is NFC-normalised.

sentences.text: आप इसे एक वीडियो देते हैं — कोई लेक्चर, कोई इंटरव्यू, कुछ भी जिसमें साफ़ आवाज़ हो — और यह वही वीडियो हिंदी में बोलता हुआ वापस देता है।
